text: This is a bicycle repair shop. Not a startup. A shop on a real street.
It has no API team. But it publishes its front desk as an agent network: one JSON file, and any assistant can talk to it.
No server. No key. Three agents and seven site actions, running in your browser.
I will ask it something a customer would actually ask.
Front desk, workshop lead, parts desk. Three agents run in this tab.
And when the workshop lead names a part, the page points at it.
The price comes from the shop's own book. Not from the model.
Two lines are not on the shelf, so it asks a different origin for stock.
My phone number stays in this tab. The trade counter gets the shop's account number, and nothing else.
Booking is a write, so the page asks first.
A receipt with an outcome. Confirmed. Not just the request returned.
Seven interoperability checks, run live on this page.
All seven pass, including the four that must be stopped.
The network is data. The runtime is mine. And the key, if there is one, never leaves this tab.
One JSON. Any assistant. The visitor's browser does the work.
